In Scenario 1, Arthur Chung knows that Teresa seems overburdened, believes she needs help, feels concerned for her well-being, and decides to offer assistance. He knows his own intention: he wants to help Teresa. He then acts on that intention by asking whether he can help and by offering to assist with her tasks.

Arthur does not know, at this point, Teresa’s deeper private reasons for hesitating, such as her possible desire to prove her capability. He also does not know the later outcomes of their collaboration or how their professional relationship will develop in future scenarios. Those are outside his knowledge in Scenario 1.

Given the main question, Arthur’s intention to help Teresa leads directly to his action of offering his assistance.
